Scaling nature-based solutions with participatory

land use and cover mapping platform

Section1.title:
Overcoming Map

Data Barriers
Section1.caption: Empower land use and land cover (LULC) planning and monitoring with intuitive tools that turn complex data into actionable maps.
Section1.item1Description: With Epistem, mapping your landscape becomes simple and powerful. Focus on the land use and land cover classes that matter most and create your own maps with user-friendly tools (no coding needed!) from publicly available satellite data.
Section1.item2Description: Creating your own land use and land cover maps is just the start. Discover how your landscape changes with Epistem's tools, providing transparent data and a consistent approach for planning and monitoring sustainable interventions.
Section1.item3Description: High-quality land use and land cover maps rely on robust reference data and mapping methodology. Through Epistem, you can access expert-processed satellite imagery, reference datasets, and mapping solutions from a community of remote-sensing enthusiasts and nature-based solutions practitioners.
Section1.item4Caption: Contribute to a growing open-source community
Section1.item4Description: Epistem platforms are built with transparent and scalable, open-source approaches. Contribute by adding or improving datasets and mapping solutions, and benefit from the community's collective power to overcome map data barriers.

Section2.title: Browse Application
Section2.caption: Explore Epistem applications to create maps, track changes, access high-quality data, and collaborate with an open-source community.
Section2.item1Subtitle:
Map past trends,

plan future action
Section2.item1Description:
Intuitive no-coding interface for creating, analysing,

and collectively acting on customizable land use and land cover map data.
Section2.item2Title: Rona (Repository for Open-source laNd use Analysis)
Section2.item2Description:
Scalable repository of participatory land use

and land cover mapping.

Section3.title: The Approach
Section3.caption: Epistem integrates scientific rigor with real-world usability, making mapping and monitoring easier, smarter, and more inclusive.
Section3.item1Description: Focuses on technical solutions that are scientifically sound, provides reliable, high-resolution data and tools grounded in research and tailored for field implementation.
Section3.item2Description: Effective solutions emerge only when those implementing change help shape the tools that drive it. Developed collaboratively with local actors and stakeholders, the system is transparent, open-source, and accessible, fostering usability and long-term ownership.
Section3.item3Description: Epistem handles complex coding and data processing behind the scenes, allowing users to generate maps and insights with ease, turning advanced science into actionable solutions.

Section4.title: About Us
Section4.caption: Supporting change-makers with data-driven solutions built for their sustainable restoration goals
Section4.description: Epistem is a consortium-led initiative combining global research expertise with local knowledge to bridge the gap between science, data, and implementation of nature-based solutions. Convened by IIASA, in partnership with CIFOR-ICRAF and WRI Indonesia, Epistem delivers practical tools for real-world impact.
Section4.item1Description: Epistem is initiated by a consortium led by the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (<a1>IIASA</a1>), in partnership with The Center for International Forestry Research and World Agroforestry (<a2>CIFOR-ICRAF</a2>) and World Resources Institute Indonesia (<a3>WRI Indonesia</a3>).
Section4.item2Description: The initiative combines global research expertise with deep local knowledge to bridge the gap between science, data, and real-world nature-based solutions.
Section4.item3Description: NbS actors often face technical barriers to accessing reliable, high-quality data that reflects diverse landscape realities. Effective NbS depend heavily on land use and land cover (LULC) data to guide planning, mobilize financial and institutional resources, and monitor implementation.
Section4.item4Description: Providing LULC data that is timely, accurate, and thematically detailed can significantly enhance the effectiveness, accountability, and impact of NbS interventions.
Section4.item5Description: Epistem strives to eliminate data barriers by providing thematically relevant, high-resolution, and accessible data tailored to diverse user needs, enabling NbS actors to focus on driving real change.
Section4.item6Description: Through a participatory approach, Epistem empowers stakeholders across the NbS delivery chain to use data that enhances planning, implementation, and monitoring throughout Indonesia and Southeast Asia.
Section4.item7Description: This data empowerment enables more sustainable and equitable land management, delivering multiple co-benefits such as:
Section4.item8Description:
• Climate change adaptation and mitigation
  • Biodiversity conservation and enhancement
  • Improved livelihoods for indigenous peoples and local communities

meta.subtitle: Mapathon Gotong Royong for Collaborative Land Use and Land Cover Mapping

summary.label: ABOUT THE EVENT
summary.title: Activity
summary.p1: The Data Democratization for Sustainable Landscapes workshop is part of the Epistem (Evolving Participatory Information System for Nature-based Climate Solutions) initiative, which aims to strengthen sustainable landscape management through a collaborative and participatory mapping approach. This activity is based on the need for accurate, open, and easily accessible land use and land cover data to support forest restoration, prevent deforestation, and achieve Indonesia's climate targets, including the 2030 FOLU Net Sink agenda.
summary.p2: Through a collaboration between IIASA, BRIN, CIFOR-ICRAF, and WRI Indonesia, Epistem has developed a web-based mapping platform called Luma Land Use Mapping for All, an open-source online mapping platform that has been tested with communities of practitioners in several regions in Indonesia and will be launched during this workshop.
summary.p3: The workshop will combine strategic presentations, technology demonstrations, hands-on practice, and map discussion sessions to build a shared understanding of modular mapping, shared reference data management, and strengthening collaborative networks across stakeholders. Commemorating National Awakening Day, the Epistem initiative aspires to instill the spirit of this national movement milestone into its vision of “data democratization for sustainable landscapes.” This moment marks a revival of collective stewardship in land use governance through mapping gotong royong—bringing together practitioners, government, and local communities to advance nature-based climate solutions.
summary.p4: The event TOR can be viewed <torlink>here</torlink>.

pressRelease.label: PRESS RELEASE
pressRelease.title: Mapping Technology That Connects People,
pressRelease.titleHighlight: Epistem Launches the Luma Mapping Platform
pressRelease.body1: Efforts toward sustainable landscape management, forest restoration, and deforestation prevention require spatial data that is accurate, open, and easily accessible to various stakeholders. To address this need, Epistem (Evolving Participatory Information System for Nature-based Climate Solutions) took the initiative to launch the online mapping platform “Luma” (Land Mapping for All) during a national workshop held in conjunction with National Awakening Day on Wednesday, May 20, at the A. A. Maramis Building in Jakarta.
pressRelease.body2: Under the theme “Revitalising Data, Preserving Land Cover,” this workshop serves as a significant milestone in marking the resurgence of national data sovereignty through cross-institutional collaboration involving practitioners, government officials, and local communities. Using a participatory approach, this event aims to introduce the Luma platform, build a national collaborative network for mapping land use and land cover, and initiate a “map forum” to strengthen synergies in support of Indonesia’s climate change mitigation agenda.
pressRelease.body3: The development of Luma is part of a collaboration between the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), the Centre for Ecological Research—National Research and Innovation Agency (PREBRIN), the Centre for International Forestry Research and World Agroforestry (CIFOR-ICRAF), and the World Resources Institute (WRI) Indonesia. This initiative is driven by the belief that resilient nature-based climate solutions stem from the availability of appropriate, inclusive mapping technologies that landscape managers can directly utilise in the field.
pressRelease.body4: In his keynote address, Andes Hamuraby Rozak, Head of the Biological and Environmental Research Organisation at BRIN, stated, “Our current challenge is not merely to protect our landscapes. It is to ensure that the decisions we make are truly based on accurate, transparent, and reliable knowledge. Because, in truth, we cannot protect what we cannot see. And we cannot make good decisions without good knowledge and data.”
pressRelease.quote1Text: Our current challenge is not merely to protect our landscapes. It is to ensure that the decisions we make are truly based on accurate, transparent, and reliable knowledge. Because, in truth, we cannot protect what we cannot see. And we cannot make good decisions without good knowledge and data.
pressRelease.quote1Role: Head of the Biological and Environmental Research Organization, BRIN
pressRelease.body5: “Landscape conservation requires map data rich in contextual information. On the other hand, technical constraints and the high costs of producing such map data have long been a classic challenge. Luma is expected to pave the way for overcoming these challenges,” said Ping Yowargana, Senior Research Scholar at IIASA
pressRelease.body6: In line with this, Andree Ekadinata, Director of the ICRAF Indonesia Program, and Asep Hidayat, Head of the Ecology Research Centre at BRIN, emphasised that the initiative launched by Epistem is an invitation to collaborate on developing landscape monitoring technologies that will support the implementation of various Nature-Based Solutions in Indonesia.
pressRelease.quote2Text: Landscape conservation requires map data rich in contextual information. On the other hand, technical constraints and the high costs of producing such map data have long been a classic challenge. Luma is expected to pave the way for overcoming these challenges.
pressRelease.body7: Luma has been piloted in South Sumatra and introduced to communities of practitioners in South Sulawesi and East Nusa Tenggara. With strategic support from BRIN and partners in these three provinces, the platform is part of the Epistem innovation ecosystem, which includes an online participatory mapping tool, a library of open-source methodologies and reference data, and a “mapathon” mechanism for collaborative analysis of land use and land cover.
pressRelease.body8: Through this approach, various stakeholders can contribute to updating land use and land cover data in a faster, more flexible, and interoperable manner. This initiative is also expected to support Indonesia’s targets outlined in the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) document and the FOLU Net Sink 2030 operational strategy, while maintaining a balance between carbon sequestration, biodiversity conservation, and improved community well-being.
pressRelease.body9: The Luma launch workshop will feature a variety of key sessions, ranging from a strategic presentation on participatory landscape management and an introduction to Epistem’s technology development philosophy to a live demonstration of Luma’s use and a discussion on the implementation of the national mapping forum. The event will also showcase the experiences of communities of practitioners from various regions who have utilised Luma in mapping activities within their respective areas.
pressRelease.body10: In addition to introducing Luma, this workshop served as a collaborative space to gather feedback on the development of Luma’s features and design, with the aim of making it more relevant to the needs of diverse user groups. Participants were also guided through the concepts of modular mapping and the development of shared reference data as the foundation for collaborative and sustainable landscape management.
pressRelease.body11: Through the launch of Luma and a series of national mapping forums, Epistem hopes to strengthen the collective effort to map Indonesia’s natural environment in a participatory manner, while also connecting people involved in safeguarding the sustainability of Indonesia’s landscapes for future generations.

Hero.title: Luma
Hero.subtitle: (Land Use Mapping for All)
Hero.caption: Turn satellite data into actionable landscape insights in quick, clear, and collaborative way.

Intro.title: Map Smarter, Not Harder
Intro.description: Luma simplifies land use and land cover (LULC) mapping into one seamless workflow. Whether you're a researcher, policymaker, or even a student, you can generate high-quality maps without technical barriers.

Features.item1Title: Generate LULC Maps in Five Simple Steps
Features.item1Desc: Transform raw satellite imagery into a classified map in minutes. Define your area of interest, select a classification scheme, evaluate model performance and thematic accuracy, then generate and export your map, all in one place.
Features.item2Desc: Go beyond mapping! Track deforestation, restoration, or other changes with built-in change detection and time series analysis tools.
Features.item3Desc: Download your maps for free or share them instantly. Luma makes collaboration straightforward and accessible.

WhyLuma.title: Why Luma?
WhyLuma.item1Desc: No coding. No specialized hardware. Just an intuitive interface built for everyone.
WhyLuma.item2Desc: Use powerful mapping tools at no cost. Ideal for individuals, students, and institutions alike.
WhyLuma.item3Desc: Built on open satellite data, Luma supports transparency, reproducibility, and collaborative innovation.
WhyLuma.item4Desc: Built on the spirit of “gotong royong”, a shared approach to building and improving maps together. Customize your maps to fit your needs while benefiting from continuous, community-driven contributions across diverse themes.
